newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yokohama says excludes DKB from being bond trustee.
newsitem.headline: Yokohama says excludes DKB from being bond trustee.

text.p: The City of Yokohama said on Thursday it has barred Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) from lead-managing or being a trustee for its municipal bonds.
An official of the city government said Yokohama had also excluded DKB from managing its public funds, but added that the bank would still be able to act as an underwriter for bond issues.

The official said a decision on whether to exclude the bank from underwriting would be taken once the financial industry's supervisory authorities decide what administrative steps will be taken against DKB.

The official said that DKB had not been involved in managing public funds for Yokohama for about the last two years. "But even if there was the possibility, we wouldn't ask the bank to do so," he said.
DKB underwrote slightly more than eight percent of Yokohama's 25 billion yen worth of bonds for June, its usual share. The subscription period for this issue started on May 23.
Top executives of DKB resigned on Friday when the bank admitted it had been unable to cut its links to racketeers in a widening saga of dubious deals and illegal payoffs.
DKB said the bank had made a total of 26 billion yen in loans to Yoshinori Koike, the younger brother of a racketeer at the heart of the Nomura Securities Co Ltd payoff scandal.
Yokohama has already excluded Nomura from underwriting its bonds, the city government official said.
